title: Sunset Strategy and Migration Playbook for Model Variants
author: Jordan Lee
body:
Purpose
This playbook defines Redwood's standard process for sunsetting (deprecating) model variants and migrating traffic/customers to successor variants or fallback models. It is intended for product managers, engineering, SRE, customer success, and legal/compliance when a model variant reaches end-of-life (EOL) or is being replaced for cost, quality, or licensing reasons.

Scope
- Applies to public and dedicated model variants listed in the Redwood model catalog.
- Excludes emergency security removals (see Incident Response Security runbook).
- Covers technical migration, billing adjustments, communications, monitoring, and rollback.

Goals and success metrics
- Minimize customer impact: <95% of active routes migrated within 30 days of migration window start.
- Quality safety net: model-output regression rate <1.0% (as measured by defined eval set).
- Availability: no increase in 99th percentile latency greater than 20% during migration windows.
- Billing correctness: 100% of migrated routes billed to the successor variant or fallback by close of billing cycle following cutover.

Preconditions (must be completed before announcing sunset)
1. Successor variant selected and validated in the staging environment.
2. Compatibility matrix completed (tokenization, supported functions/tool-calling, max sequence length).
3. Regression test report (eval harness) showing parity or documented deltas and mitigation.
4. Billing mapping defined (old variant -> new variant / credit conversion).
5. Customer-impact list exported (active tenants, routes, critical SLAs).
6. Legal review complete for licensing changes.

Timeline and Phase Checklist
- Phase 0: Planning (T-60 to T-30 days)
  - Owner: Product PM
  - Tasks: select successor, run regression/eval, prepare compatibility matrix, draft customer notice, schedule SRE/CS working session.
- Phase 1: Announcement (T-30 days)
  - Owner: Go-to-market & CS
  - Tasks: send formal notice to affected customers, publish public deprecation notice page, set in-console sunset banner for impacted routes.
- Phase 2: Migration Window (T-30 to T+30 days)
  - Owner: CS + Engineering
  - Tasks: enable migration tooling, assist customers with testing, open migration tickets, monitor KPIs.
- Phase 3: Cutover & Billing Transition (T+30 days)
  - Owner: Billing + SRE
  - Tasks: automated cutover of non-responsive tenants (if allowed), finalize billing mapping, update catalog.
- Phase 4: Post-Cutover (T+30 to T+60 days)
  - Owner: Product + SRE
  - Tasks: collect telemetry, run postmortem, remove variant from public catalog, archive artifacts.

Ownership and escalation
- Product PM: overall program owner, stakeholder communication, final approval for cutover.
- Eng-SRE: migration tooling, routing policies, automated fallback flow.
- Customer Success: coordinate customer migration plans, SLA negotiation, issue triage.
- Billing & Finance: price/credit mapping, invoice adjustments, reconciliation.
- Legal & Security: confirm compliance and license termination conditions.
- Escalation: Pager duty for Migration SRE rotation; create incident channel #migration-eol in Slack.

Communication templates (shortened)
- Customer Notice Subject: Important: Redwood is retiring model variant [VARIANT_NAME] on [DATE]
- Body: "We are retiring [VARIANT_NAME] on [DATE]. Your routes using this variant will be able to switch to [SUCCESSOR_NAME] with identical API contracts. If you prefer, Redwood will schedule a migration session with your CS representative. Details: [link to migration guide]."
- In-console banner: "[VARIANT_NAME] will be retired on [DATE]. Click to view migration options."

Technical migration steps (engineers)
1. Validate that successor model variant is compatible:
   - Tokenizer check: ensure same token mapping for sentinel tokens.
   - Function/tool compatibility: run smoke tests for tool-calls and streaming.
2. Create a migration plan for each tenant route (RouteID list).
3. Use migration API (example):
   - curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/migrations \
     -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"route_ids": ["route-123"], "from_variant": "v1-small-quant", "to_variant": "v2-core-q4", "dry_run": true}'
4. Run dry-run and collect perf/quality samples into /tmp/migration-samples.
5. If dry-run passes, schedule a canary subset (5% traffic) and observe for 48 hours.

Canary and rollback policy
- Canary size: default 5% of traffic or up to 3 enterprise tenants (whichever smaller).
- Canary SLO gates (must pass to expand):
  - 99th percentile latency increase < 15%.
  - Error rate increase < 0.5% absolute.
  - Eval regression delta < 0.5% in key prompt set.
- Rollback triggers:
  - Any customer-impacting error > 1% for 15 minutes.
  - Quality regressions discovered by CS for a paying tenant.
- Rollback process:
  1. Pause migration orchestration.
  2. Re-route canary traffic back to previous variant.
  3. Open an incident and assign to migration SRE.
  4. Product to convene mitigation review within 8 hours.

Monitoring and dashboards
- Minimum dashboards to create/update prior to migration:
  - Migration progress dashboard (routes migrated, percent complete).
  - Per-variant latency & error heatmap.
  - Customer-impact dashboard (top 10 tenants by errors during migration).
- Example queries (PromQL-like pseudo):
  - error_rate_by_variant = sum(rate(request_errors_total{variant!=""}[5m])) by (variant) / sum(rate(requests_total[5m])) by (variant)
  - p99_latency_migration = histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{migration_window="true"}[5m])) by (le, variant))
- Alerts:
  - migration_error_rate_high: alert if error_rate_by_variant for successor > 1.5x baseline for 10m.
  - migration_latency_regression: alert if p99_latency_migration > baseline_p99 * 1.2 for 15m.

Billing & credits handling
| Scenario | Action | Owner | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Customer migrates voluntarily before cutover | Bill successor variant from migration date | Billing | Preserve prorated credits where applicable |
| Customer remains on deprecated variant after window (no response) | Auto-migrate to fallback variant if policy allows; otherwise disable route per contract | Product + Legal | For enterprise, require explicit approval before disabling |
| Pricing changes between variants | Issue pro-rated invoice adjustment or one-time credit | Finance | Communicate in announcement letter |

Data retention and audit
- Archive logs and sample outputs for all migration dry-runs and canaries for 90 days in the migrations bucket: s3://redwood-archives/migrations/{variant}/{date}/.
- Export audit trail: who performed migration, timestamp, tool versions. This must be attached to the migration ticket.

Postmortem and learning loop
- Owner: Product PM
- Deliverable within 14 days of cutover: Postmortem doc with root cause, impact, mitigations, and action items. Include customer feedback summary.
- Feed action items into roadmap: tag as high/med/low and assign owners.

Operational playbook quick checklist (for on-call)
- Verify migration window is active and banners are visible.
- Confirm SRE migration job queue is empty after cutover.
- Validate billing mapping for at least 3 customers.
- Run smoke test script against 10 migrated routes.

Appendix A — Example migration CLI snippets
- Dry run:
  redwoodctl migrate --routes-file routes.csv --from v1-small-quant --to v2-core-q4 --dry-run --output migration-report.json
- Execute migration (canary 5%):
  redwoodctl migrate --routes-file routes.csv --from v1-small-quant --to v2-core-q4 --canary 5 --notify cs-team

Appendix B — Communication timeline checklist
1. T-30: Email notice and in-console banner (public doc published).
2. T-21: Host migration office hours (recording linked).
3. T-7: Reminder; targeted outreach to high-usage tenants.
4. Cutover: Final confirmation 24 hours before.
5. T+7: Follow-up with migrated customers and CS satisfaction survey.

FAQ (select)
- Q: Can customers opt-out of auto-migration?
  A: Enterprise customers can request an exception; it requires a signed amendment. Self-serve customers are subject to the public policy.
- Q: Are token counts preserved across variants?
  A: Tokenization differences are listed in the compatibility matrix; migration tooling rewrites static prompt templates where safe.

Document maintenance
- Review cadence: annual or whenever a major serving change occurs.
- Next scheduled review: 2027-09-20.
